newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone troops, hunters, kill for diamonds.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone troops, hunters, kill for diamonds.

text.p: Twenty soldiers and hunters in central Sierra Leone have died in pitched battles over diamonds, military sources said on Tuesday.

The two groups are allies against rebels in the West African country but shooting broke out on Sunday and continued on Monday at diamond-rich Tongofield, sparking an exodus by thousands of townspeople.
Residents in nearby Kenema told Reuters by telephone the local hunters, known as Kamajors, objected when soldiers started digging in a gravel pit where diamonds are often found.
"The Kamajors told the soldiers they had no right to dig for diamonds on their lands. The soldiers refused and this sparked off the fighting," one resident said.
Military sources said 20 bodies had arrived in Kenema by Tuesday as the search for more continued.
Foreign relief workers in Kenema said 15 people injured in the clashes had arrived along with thousands of civilians from the Tongofield area.
Sierra Leone's deputy president, Albert Demby, arrived in Tongofield on Monday with senior army officers to arrange a truce between the soldiers and Kamajors.
"The fighting has died down," a government source in the capital Freetown said.
